This work is implemented using PyTorch (Paszke et al., 2019 ) , an open-source deep learning framework licensed under the BSD license, and the Hugging Face Transformers library (Wolf et al., 2019 ) , licensed under Apache 2.0. All software usage complies with their respective license terms. For evaluation, we use CountBench Paiss et al. ( 2023 ) and Visual CounterFact Golovanevsky et al. ( 2025a ) licensed under the Apache 2.0 license. We evaluate a three diverse VLMs. Table 5 provides details on the open-source models used in our experiments. These models are sourced from Hugging Face, with their specific repository paths listed for reproducibility. We use CountBench Paiss et al. ( 2023 ) for our counting task and Visual CounterFact Golovanevsky et al. ( 2025a ) for our color identification task. CountBench consists of 491 text-image pairs. We adapt CountBench using our novel misaligned prompts, yielding a total of 3,437 image-prompt pairs. We use the “color” split of the Visual CounterFact dataset, which comprises 493 base-image-label pairs. We adapt Visual CounterFact with our base and misaligned prompts, yielding 2,465 image-prompt pairs. For each image with ground-truth object count N N , we first present the model with a baseline prompt , P B = P_{B}= “How many [objects] are there in the image?”, and retain only samples for which the model correctly predicts N N .
